maintainer: TIGER-Lab (Wang, Ma, Zhang et al., Wenhu Chen); official leaderboard on Hugging Face
measures: Graduate-level multitask knowledge and reasoning: 12,000 questions across 14 domains, 10 answer options, reasoning-heavy; extends/supersedes MMLU
notes: Gemini 3.8 Flash and Claude Opus 5 values are Vals AI runs displayed by BenchLM. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 74.1 is a vendor claim (DeepSeek model card base table, quoted by BenchLM). Successor of MMLU, which is saturated (97-99% frontier, benchlm.ai/blog/posts/mmlu-vs-mmlu-pro); no distinct post-MMLU-Pro successor found in this pass; global variant GMMLU exists (Claude Opus 5 94.3%, llm-stats). Public dataset since 2024 derived from public sources, multiple trackers report nearing saturation - contamination risk high. No A-scope benchmark maps directly to the six F-02 dimensions; knowledge/reasoning dimension is POSSIBLE_FUTURE_DIMENSION.

maintainer: Rein et al. (NYU); independent public result pages by Epoch AI and Artificial Analysis
measures: 198 hardest graduate-level physics/chemistry/biology multiple-choice questions, expert-written and verified, designed to be Google-proof; scientific reasoning
notes: Claude Opus 5 93.4% is a Vals AI run displayed by BenchLM. Mistral Medium 3.5 74.8% is an aggregator figure (requesty.ai; benchmarklist.com corroborates 74.8); Mistral's own card publishes no GPQA figure. IntuitionLabs (94.1% for Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview) cites the Artificial Analysis leaderboard. Dataset released password-protected with a canary string (Epoch AI page) - contamination risk low, though the top of the leaderboard is clustered within ~1.2 points (BenchLM AA-GPQA page), i.e. nearing saturation. Human baselines: PhD specialists ~65-70%.

measures: Abstract visual reasoning on novel grid puzzles (ARC core); fluid intelligence and skill acquisition; reported with a cost-per-task efficiency metric
notes: Semi-Private scores, all verified runs on the official ARC Prize leaderboard (v1 column). v1 is saturated at the top and superseded by ARC-AGI-2/3 - status stale. Contamination risk high: the public training set has been available for years, and the ARC-AGI 3 paper (as reported in community discussion of the leaderboard) alleges frontier models, including Gemini 3, memorized tasks similar to v1/v2; treat as an allegation, not a finding. Model strings recorded exactly as the leaderboard writes them (effort in parentheses).

measures: Next-generation abstract reasoning: harder novel grid puzzles stressing state-of-the-art reasoning, with human calibration (400+ participants) and a cost efficiency metric
notes: Semi-Private verified scores from the official leaderboard (v2 column), except Claude Opus 5 90.4% from its ARC Prize results page (Max reasoning effort). Per-model result pages exist, e.g. https://arcprize.org/results/anthropic-claude-opus-5-5 (Opus 5.5: 91.7% Max, 92.5% XHigh, 93.3% High on v2 Semi-Private). Mistral Medium 3.5 has no ARC-AGI entry on the leaderboard - stays unknown. Contamination medium: semi-private eval set, but the ARC-AGI 3 paper (as reported in community discussion) alleges memorization of similar tasks for v1/v2 scores; allegation, not a finding. llm-stats lists GPT-6 Astra at 0.950 on ARC-AGI v2, consistent with the official 95.0%.

measures: Hardest current ARC generation: novel reasoning tasks where standard-effort runs cost thousands of dollars per task; efficiency (cost per task) is part of the reported result
notes: Standard-harness verified scores (Standard column; GPT-6 Astra Max also lists 98.6% at $17.3K/task on a Provider Adapter, recorded on the leaderboard separately). BenchLM corroborates the same top three (GPT-6 Astra 62.7%, Claude Opus 5 30.2%, Gemini 3.8 Flash 10.4%, benchlm.ai/benchmarks/arcagi3, Sep 24 2026). New, privately held task set with very high run costs - contamination risk low. GPT-5.6 Sol tops out at 7.8% (Max) and Terra at 0.8% on the official leaderboard.

maintainer: Scale AI (Scale Labs) together with the Center for AI Safety (CAIS)
measures: 2,500 of the hardest expert-vetted, subject-diverse, multimodal closed-ended academic questions; pass@1 with LLM-graded answers; designed to resist benchmark saturation

scores.model: Claude Opus 5.5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Default Fallback)
Claude Fable 5.1 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Default Fallback)

notes: BenchLM row (65% for Claude Fable 5.1, Sep 27 2026) covers a different protocol mix than Artificial Analysis; BenchLM explicitly keeps tool-assisted and closed-book HLE runs separate, so the 65% and the AA 59.1% are not directly comparable. Gemini 3.8 Flash 54.9% is a vendor claim (HLE-Verified, Google's announcement table as quoted by third-party coverage). CAIS released an HLE-Rolling fork on Sep 17 2026 that is continually cleaned - the rolling refresh is why contamination stays medium rather than high. Vals.ai reports refusal-fallback effects on HLE-style academic benchmarks for Claude (Opus 5 example), so fallback composition matters when comparing rows.

maintainer: Mathematical Association of America (competition); benchmark usage and leaderboards are community/aggregator-maintained
measures: 30 integer-answer olympiad mathematics problems (two 15-problem sittings) from the 2025 American Invitational Mathematics Examination; pass@1
notes: Status stale: a fixed February 2025 exam, saturated at the top (multiple leaders at 100%) and superseded by harder math benchmarks (sources note reasoning-model saturation of AIME-class benchmarks; Epoch AI tracks FrontierMath tiers as successors). Contamination risk high: the problems have been public since early 2025 and are widely present in training corpora. No ladder-specific Opus 5.5 / Gemini 3.8 / Mistral Medium 3.5 AIME 2025 row was found in this pass - unknown, not invented.

maintainer: Allen Institute for AI (Ai2; Nouha Dziri and colleagues)
measures: Controlled mathematical-reasoning generalization along three axes (exploratory, compositional, transformative) across six domains, using 40 templated problem generators; also used to study RL (GRPO) effects on generalization
notes: Scores stay unknown: the Ai2 announcement (June 24 2025) names the evaluated models (DeepSeek-R1, Claude 3.7, OpenAI o3-mini, o4-mini, and GRPO-tuned Qwen2.5-7B variants) but publishes no per-model score table on the accessed page, and no maintained public leaderboard was found in this pass. Templated generation with controlled train/test splits keeps contamination risk low. Status unknown rather than active: no evidence of ongoing maintenance was found. Qualitative findings only: accuracy degrades sharply with problem complexity; ~38% of DeepSeek-R1's incorrect responses initially contained the correct answer before self-correction.

maintainer: SWE-bench team (Jimenez et al.); Verified is the 500-task human-reviewed subset co-released with OpenAI researchers
measures: Resolving real GitHub issues in Python repositories: model writes a patch that must pass the issue's fail-to-pass tests; the most-cited coding-agent benchmark
notes: Vendor claims marked per source: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max 80.6% is DeepSeek's own April 2026 launch number (morphllm coverage); Mistral Medium 3.5 77.6% is Mistral's model-card claim (mirrored on ollama.com). Claude Opus 5 has no Anthropic-reported SWE-bench number (morphllm); the 97.00% is a Vals.ai run tracked by steel.dev. Contamination risk high: tasks come from public pre-cutoff GitHub issues, and Scale AI positions its newer SWE-bench Pro as the contamination-resistant alternative; vendor-scaffold numbers routinely exceed standardized-harness numbers by wide margins (Fable 5 ~80% vendor vs Muse Spark 1.1 61.5% top on Scale SEAL).

measures: 300-task subset of SWE-bench Full; same issue-resolving task, lighter eval cost
notes: Same construction and exposure as SWE-bench Full/Verified, hence contamination risk high. Fewer ladder-model rows were found for Lite than for Verified in this pass; ladder models without a public Lite row stay unknown. Largely superseded by Verified in 2026 reporting.

measures: Resolving 300 curated real-world GitHub pull-request tasks across 42 repositories in 9 programming languages (C, C++, Go, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, PHP, Ruby, Rust)
notes: Claude Opus 5.5 93.9% appears in llm-stats comparison tables (Anthropic system-card figures). Claude Mythos Preview 0.873 leads the llm-stats aggregate (34 models). Harder than SWE-bench Verified with a wider performance spread (launch discussion on r/LocalLLaMA). Public PR-derived tasks - contamination risk high.

maintainer: SWE-bench team (integrated into the SWE-bench repository Jan 13 2025)
measures: SWE-bench issue resolution with visual context (screenshots, design mockups) added to issue descriptions
notes: Very thin coverage: llm-stats lists 5 evaluated models, all self-reported; BenchLM lists 4 (display-only, excluded from its rankings). Claude Opus 5.5 0.614 is the llm-stats leader. Contamination risk high by construction (public repos plus public visual artifacts).

measures: Larger contamination-resistant SWE benchmark from more recent tasks, run on Scale's standardized SEAL harness; public and private (held-out) subsets
notes: Claude Opus 5.5 0.899 leads the llm-stats aggregate (59 models); Claude Opus 4.8 69.2% and Gemini 3.8 Flash 61.6% are vendor-run figures (morphllm keeps a SEAL-dagger distinction; DataCamp quotes Google's announcement table), while Muse Spark 1.1 61.5% is the top score on Scale's standardized SEAL board (Aug 2026). The vendor-vs-standardized gap is the largest of any benchmark in this catalog. Contamination risk low: Scale's positioning is contamination resistance, plus a held-out private subset.

maintainer: LiveCodeBench team (paper: Holistic and Contamination Free Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code)
measures: Competitive programming (LeetCode, AtCoder, Codeforces) collected continuously over time windows; code generation; designed contamination-free with delayed public release
notes: DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Max 93.5 Pass@1 is a vendor claim from the April 2026 launch (morphllm flags it as vendor-run); llm-stats lists it as leader at 0.935 across 75 models. Contamination risk low by design (time-windowed collection, delayed public release per BenchLM). Dimension: the F-02 frame names this skill D-ALGO (algorithmic coding); the launch enum has no D-ALGO, so it is recorded as D-IMPL. Multiple dataset versions exist (Kaggle notes versioning), so rows are comparable only within a version.

maintainer: OpenAI (benchmark data, automated grading workflow, public leaderboard via GitHub Pages)
measures: 1,400+ real freelance software engineering tasks from Upwork valued at $1M USD in real payouts; both IC coding tasks and manager tasks, scored by end-to-end tests and payout value
notes: Very thin third-party coverage: llm-stats lists 4 models on the full benchmark, all self-reported. GPT-5 1.000 is on the IC-Diamond subset only (6 models). F-02 names SWE-Lancer Manager as the sole public D-CRIT (adversarial review) proxy, at most WEAK; the IC subset maps to D-IMPL. Contamination risk unknown: tasks are real past Upwork jobs published in the repository, but no contamination study was found in this pass (contamination studies are collector B's scope).

maintainer: XLang Lab (verified-leaderboard maintainers named on the site)
measures: 369 real computer tasks (361 excluding Google Drive tasks) involving real web and desktop apps, OS file I/O and cross-application workflows on Windows/macOS/Ubuntu; multimodal agents, execution-verified
notes: Verified-leaderboard rows (BenchLM OSWorld-Verified, Sep 22 2026; the official verified leaderboard requires a maintainer-run session). OSWorld 2.0 is a newer, harder variant with separate scores: vendor-reported coverage puts Gemini 3.8 Flash at 59.0% and Claude Opus 5 at ~75.4% on OSWorld-2.0 (Google's table as quoted by third parties); scores are not comparable across variants. steel.dev tracks 21 OSWorld and 22 OSWorld 2.0 sourced results. Dimension D-DEBUG per the launch enum corresponds to F-02 D-TERM (terminal/autonomous execution). Contamination risk low: dynamic real environments with execution-based verification.

measures: Tool-agent-user interaction in realistic domains (retail, airline, telecom, banking, knowledge): dual-control simulation where agent and (simulated) user both act on a shared world state; average pass rate across domains
notes: GLM-5.2 99.1% is the highest published tau2 score (BenchLM compiled ledger, 151 models) but BenchLM itself warns the available coverage and evaluation setups do not establish comparability; pricepertoken lists the same 99.1% (Aug 16 2026). Gemini 3.7 Flash 80.6% is the OpenRouter tau2-Bench Airline leaderboard leader (snapshot 2026-09-27). Mistral Medium 3.5 94.2% is an aggregator figure (requesty.ai); Mistral's own model card claims 91.4% on the newer tau3-Telecom instead. tau2-bench v1.0.1 (July 2026) fixed banking_knowledge grading: results before and after are not comparable. tau3 exists; tau-bench.com hosts the official leaderboard. Dimension D-DEBUG (launch enum) corresponds to F-02 D-TERM autonomous execution.

maintainer: gaia-benchmark (Meta-FAIR and collaborators); leaderboard is a Hugging Face Space with server-side scoring
measures: 466 real-world assistant questions across three difficulty levels: multi-step reasoning, web browsing, tool use and multimodal understanding; exact-match scoring against withheld answers
notes: Scores are agent/system setups, not bare models, except GPT-5 Mini (bare-model board). The same benchmark shows very different numbers depending on the harness (rapidclaw documents 74.6% Princeton HAL vs 52.3% BenchLM vs 44.8% bare-model for different leaders), so cross-board comparison is invalid. Humans score around 92%. Test answers are withheld and scoring is server-side - contamination risk low. GAIA is at best a weak proxy for F-02 D-SYN (multi-document synthesis); recorded as POSSIBLE_FUTURE_DIMENSION.
